subject: Wiener Diffusion Model - multiple constrains for the same parameter

messages.author: 57c061923b38e1e8
messages.subject: Wiener Diffusion Model - multiple constrains for the same parameter
parts:
Hello everyone, 

I am currently working on a hierarchical version of the wiener diffusion model and I am having some issues with the non-decision time parameter. Since I am trying to estimate one parameter per trial, the estimated non-decision time parameter can't be higher then the actual response time for that trial. If the boundary is not specified in the model, rstan won't start sampling.  

However, since different trials have different response times, I would like to know if there is a way in which I could parameterize the model so that the upper constrain for trial "n" is either given by a function 

data{
int  N;  // number of  trials
y[N];  //Reaction times
...
}

parameters{
for (i in 1:N){
vector<lower=0.0001, upper = y[n] - .01>[N] tau; //non-decision time for trial n
    }
...
}  

or by a value from a vector?

data{
int  N;  // number of  trials
real y[N];  //Reaction times
int upper_limit[N]; //upper_limit = y[n] - 0.01
...
}

parameters{
for (i in 1:N){
vector<lower=0.0001, upper = upper_limit[n]>[N] tau; //non-decision time for trial n
    }
...
}

Thank you, 

Tiago

> }

and apply the log Jacobian adjustment manually on each component.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Wiener Diffusion Model - multiple constrains for the same parameter
parts: It is un-Bayesian to make the bounds on parameters depend on the outcome that is purportedly generated by those parameters. Just make the starting values be smaller with init_r or by specifying the starting values.

messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: Wiener Diffusion Model - multiple constrains for the same parameter
parts:
The non-decision time parameter is notoriously difficult to estimate.
The first thing I would do is to remove obvious outlier (fast) RTs.
If you are uncomfortable with a simple cut-off approach, the dmat toolbox (Matlab) has a nifty approach.

Otherwise, people have been advocating to use a mixture model (see eg the HDDM toolbox in Python), such that the likelihood has these two parts:
- the wiener pdf
- a uniform that spans all possible Date

Let's say you fix your mixture to 95% wiener and 5% uniform.
Then, in pseudo code

target += log(.05*exp(uniform_lpdf(y|alpha, beta)) + .95*exp(wiener_lpdf(y|alpha_w,tau_w,beta_w,delta_w))

Or using log_sum_exp

log05 = log(.05)
log95 = log(.05)
target += log_sum_exp(log05 + uniform_lpdf(y|alpha, beta), log95 + wiener_lpdf(y|alpha_w,tau_w,beta_w,delta_w)

Let me know if this works, I haven't been able to test this.

Guido
